page: Microsoft Azure E48s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is configured with 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI extensions, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic accelerators. The instance features 384.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. It includes no bundled local storage and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote attached storage for disk persistence.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput in memory-intensive operations. The instance achieved 250.5 GB/sec in large-block uncached read memory bandwidth and 126.78 GB/sec in uncached write memory bandwidth, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Cached small-block memory reads reached 2072.65 GB/sec. General compute metrics fall predominantly in the middle 50 percent category, with a PassMark CPU score of 38554.05, a Geekbench multi-core score of 13756.0, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 44701.21. In-memory data throughput is demonstrated by 38.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 38.01 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

The primary tradeoff of the E48s_v4 lies in workloads constrained by raw single-thread speed or compute-bound inference tasks. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and generative LLM text generation metrics both registered in the bottom 25 percent. In terms of cost efficiency, the instance provides high memory density per core, making it an efficient allocation for architectures where RAM capacity and uncached memory bandwidth dominate requirements. It is well suited for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caches, big data processing frameworks, and high-concurrency static web serving.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, it supplies 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores and 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU allocation. The hardware platform includes AVX-512 VNNI extensions and 35 MB of L3 cache, with no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong performance in uncached memory bandwidth, achieving 250.5 GB/sec read and 126.78 GB/sec write throughput. General compute and in-memory operations remain balanced, reflected by 38.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 38.01 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Because single-thread decompression and LLM token generation exhibit lower relative throughput, the instance offers the best operational efficiency for large in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, and memory-constrained analytical pipelines.
